title: Sell Mineral Rights in Cairo, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Cairo, WV | Ritchie County
metaDescription: Cairo, WV sits in historic Ritchie County oil country, near old Petroleum boomtown ground. We buy legacy and modern mineral interests here directly.
heroLead: Cairo sits along the North Bend Rail Trail in Ritchie County, a few miles from what was once the boomtown of Petroleum, and the mineral tracts around it carry some of the oldest continuously producing oil leases in the state.
intro: Ritchie County's oil history predates the Marcellus play by well over a century, and Cairo's tracts often show it: shallow Big Injun and Gordon sand wells still nominally pumping under leases that were negotiated when a barrel of oil sold for a fraction of today's price. Modern operators have since layered Marcellus and Utica/Point Pleasant leasing on top of that legacy production.

We buy mineral and royalty interests around Cairo directly, reading both the old shallow lease and any newer deep-rights lease on your tract before making an offer, since the two rarely share the same terms.

sections.heading: A century of layered leasing
paragraphs: It's common near Cairo for a single family tract to carry a shallow oil or gas lease dating to the early or mid-twentieth century alongside a Marcellus or Utica lease signed within the last fifteen years. Each pays under its own terms, and one can be a flat-rate lease while the other pays a modern royalty percentage.

sections.heading: Flat-rate leases from the shallow-well era
paragraphs: Many of Ritchie County's oldest leases predate West Virginia's statutory minimum one-eighth royalty for flat-rate leases. If your family's Cairo-area lease was never converted, you may still be receiving the same modest flat payment set decades ago. We check whether conversion applies before pricing the interest.

sections.heading: Heirship on century-old family tracts
paragraphs: Tracts with this much history have usually split across four or five generations of heirs. It's routine to find a Cairo-area mineral interest owned by a dozen people, several with no idea the interest still exists. We buy individual fractional shares and handle the chain-of-title work ourselves.

faqs.question: My family's Cairo lease is over a hundred years old. Is it still valid?
faqs.answer: Many legacy leases remain in effect as long as production, or a substitute like shut-in payments, continues under the lease terms. We review the specific lease and current well status.

faqs.question: Do I get separate royalty from the old well and the new Marcellus well?
faqs.answer: If both are active and both cover your tract, yes, each pays under its own lease or unit order, tracked separately.

faqs.question: How many heirs typically share a Cairo-area interest?
faqs.answer: It varies, but tracts with a century of history commonly have six to a dozen or more co-owners. We can buy an individual share without requiring the others to sell.
